::: {#def-single-world .theorem}
## Single-world independence

For every value $\mathbf v$ of $\mathbf V$, let $\Gamma_{\mathbf v}$ be the static regime that sets every variable to its value in $\mathbf v$. The counterfactual variables of $(\mathcal M, \mathcal M^{(\Gamma_{\mathbf v})})$, obtained by sequential substitution,

$$
\big\{\, V^{(\Gamma_{\mathbf v})} : V \in \mathbf V \,\big\},
$$

are mutually independent. Each $V^{(\Gamma_{\mathbf v})}$ depends on $\mathbf v$ only through the values $\mathbf{pa}_V$ of $V$'s parents, and is written $V^{(\mathbf{pa}_V)}$.
:::
